notes: EBIT definition: used GAAP ‘Operating income (loss)’ from GM’s consolidated income statements as EBIT. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1467858/000146785826000013/gm-20251231.htm))

D&A: used ‘Depreciation and amortization expense’ (excluding impairment charges per the line item) from GM’s notes/financial disclosures and converted from ‘(In millions)’ to full USD units. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1467858/000146785826000013/gm-20251231.htm))

Capex: used cash flow line ‘Expenditures for property’ as capex and converted from ‘(In millions)’ to full USD units. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1467858/000146785826000013/gm-20251231.htm))

NWC construct: computed from consolidated balance sheet ‘Total current assets’ minus ‘Cash and cash equivalents’ and ‘Marketable debt securities’, less consolidated ‘Total current liabilities’ minus ‘Short-term debt and current portion of long-term debt’ (so NWC excludes debt and cash/near-cash; working capital includes GM Financial receivables given consolidated reporting). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1467858/000146785826000013/gm-20251231.htm))
Tax rate: set to a normalized rate proxy using GM’s ETR-adjusted effective tax rate for 2025 (18.9%). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1467858/000146785826000013/gm-20251231.htm))
WACC and terminal assumptions are model inputs assumed for DCF (not disclosed as single-point inputs in GM filings/press materials).

NOL fields: gross NOL carryforward amounts and NOL utilization percent are not provided in a directly usable single number; GM discloses deferred tax assets and carryforward-related components, so `nol_balance` and `nol_utilization_pct` are set to null.

catalysts: Further normalization of consolidated GAAP operating income as non-recurring EV-related charges fade and cost actions flow through.
North America and services operating performance (pricing discipline, subscriber growth, and renewal rates) supporting higher sustainable EBIT margins.
Changes to tariffs/trade policy and commodity/input cost trends driving margin variability versus base-case.
company_overview: GM is a global automaker with major brands (Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, GMC) and a significant captive financing arm (GM Financial).
The company is transitioning its vehicle portfolio while also monetizing technology-driven services (e.g., OnStar and Super Cruise).

In its FY2025 reporting, GM emphasized EV capacity right-sizing and cost discipline following special charges in 2025. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/gm-releases-2025-financial-results-and-2026-guidance-board-declares-dividend-at-20-higher-quarterly-rate-and-approves-new-6-0-billion-share-repurchase-authorization-302670831.html))
current_context: FY2025 results: net income attributable to stockholders of $2.7B and EBIT-adjusted of $12.7B; Q4 net income included large special charges tied to EV capacity realignment. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/gm-releases-2025-financial-results-and-2026-guidance-board-declares-dividend-at-20-higher-quarterly-rate-and-approves-new-6-0-billion-share-repurchase-authorization-302670831.html))

2026 guidance: EBIT-adjusted $13.0B–$15.0B and capital spending $10.0B–$12.0B (inclusive of battery cell manufacturing joint ventures). ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/gm-releases-2025-financial-results-and-2026-guidance-board-declares-dividend-at-20-higher-quarterly-rate-and-approves-new-6-0-billion-share-repurchase-authorization-302670831.html))

GM reported record OnStar subscriber levels (12M global subscribers) and strong Super Cruise growth (to 620k+). ([news.gm.com](https://news.gm.com/home.detail.html/Pages/news/us/en/2026/jan/0127-GM-letter-shareholders-Q4-2025.html))
investment_highlights: Base-case assumes GAAP operating performance normalizes from 2025 special-charge impact toward a mid-cycle EBIT margin profile (margin recovery rather than perpetual peak margins). ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/gm-releases-2025-financial-results-and-2026-guidance-board-declares-dividend-at-20-higher-quarterly-rate-and-approves-new-6-0-billion-share-repurchase-authorization-302670831.html))
Revenue growth is modeled modestly (not industry-leading), consistent with a mature auto demand environment and incremental market share assumptions.

Reinvestment intensity in the base-case (capex as a percent of sales) is calibrated to 2026 management capital spending guidance as a reality check. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/gm-releases-2025-financial-results-and-2026-guidance-board-declares-dividend-at-20-higher-quarterly-rate-and-approves-new-6-0-billion-share-repurchase-authorization-302670831.html))
Working-capital intensity is held near recent levels to reflect consolidated balance-sheet dynamics, including GM Financial receivables, within the model’s NWC construct.
key_risks: Downside risk from EV demand shortfalls and/or additional impairments/restructuring charges that depress GAAP EBIT below the normalized path.
Auto industry cyclicality and funding/credit conditions impacting GM Financial’s earnings and working capital.
Labor, pensions, and other fixed-cost pressures limiting margin recovery even if volumes stabilize.

valuation_summary: DCF inputs use FY2023–FY2025 GAAP operating income as EBIT and convert filing ‘Depreciation and amortization expense’ and ‘Expenditures for property’ into full currency units. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1467858/000146785826000013/gm-20251231.htm))

Terminal value uses a conservative Gordon growth approach (terminal growth below nominal long-run economic growth) rather than an aggressive exit multiple.
